ai.description: The Mandalay Kukri Snake reaches 50 cm. It is brownish-grey with a dark, V-shaped nape mark and a pale, unpatterned belly. Key features include a blunt snout and enlarged, blade-like rear teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Oligodon theobaldi* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of 15–19 dark, V-shaped or chevron-like crossbars that lack the distinct pale borders seen in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Mandalay Kukri Snake inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands, typically found at elevations ranging from lowlands up to approximately 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Mandalay Kukri snake is primarily nocturnal, using its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice into reptile eggs, which are a primary component of its diet.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon theobaldi* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, typically from April to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Mandalay Kukri Snake is found in Northeast India (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur) and Myanmar, typically inhabiting tropical forests at low to moderate elevations.
